'''Gilbert Daniel Nessim''' ({{langx|he|גילברט דניאל נסים}}; born 31 January 1966) is a [[chemistry]] professor at [[Bar-Ilan University]] specializing in the [[Chemical synthesis|synthesis]] of 1D and 2D [[nanomaterials]] for [[Electronics|electronic]], mechanic, and [[energy]] applications.<ref name=BIU-chemistry>[https://ch.biu.ac.il/nessim Nessim's Lab, Chemistry department - Bar-Ilan University]</ref>

==Biography==
Gilbert Daniel Nessim was born in [[Milan]], in 1966. He earned two Master of Sciences in [[Electrical Engineering]] ([[MSEE|Master of Engineering]]), the first in 1989 from the [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] (Politecnico di Milano), Italy and the second in 1991 from [[École Centrale Paris]], France within the [[Erasmus Programme|Erasmus]] / T.I.M.E. program ([[Top International Managers in Engineering]]). He completed [[Master of Advanced Studies#France and francophone countries|D.E.A. (Diplôme d’études Approfondies)]] in [[optoelectronics]] in 1991 from the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI), France with distinction. After graduation, he worked for three years at [[Otis Worldwide|Otis Elevators]] in their European Research and Development center in France where he developed and patented an innovative electronic infrared detector for elevator doors. Later in 1994, he earned an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] from [[INSEAD]], France with a [[Giovanni Agnelli]] scholarship. Following his MBA, Nessim joined an American consulting firm, [[PRTM]] (now acquired by PwC, [[PricewaterhouseCoopers]]), as a consultant, assisting in product development and operations strategy to various hi-tech companies in Europe and USA.<ref name=BIU-chemistry />
    
In 2004, he started his PhD at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in [[Material Science]] and Engineering. Under the supervision of Professor [[Carl V. Thompson]],<ref name=MIT>[https://mmns.scripts.mit.edu/index.php/people/carl-v-thomspon#&ts=undefined Carl V. Thompson, MIT]</ref> he focused his research on the synthesis of [[carbon nanotubes]].<ref name="NessimAcquaviva2010">{{cite journal|last1=Nessim|first1=Gilbert D.|last2=Acquaviva|first2=Donatello|last3=Seita|first3=Matteo|last4=O'Brien|first4=Kevin P.|last5=Thompson|first5=Carl V.|title=The Critical Role of the Underlayer Material and Thickness in Growing Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanotubes and Nanofibers on Metallic Substrates by Chemical Vapor Deposition|journal=Advanced Functional Materials|volume=20|issue=8|year=2010|pages=1306–1312|issn=1616-301X|doi=10.1002/adfm.200902265|s2cid=97005659 }}</ref> He then spent a year as a postdoc in a collaborative project between Professor Carl V. Thompson (MIT) and Professor [[Doron Aurbach]] (Bar-Ilan University, Israel). In 2010, he joined the staff of the Chemistry Department of [[Bar-Ilan University]] where he became {{when|date=August 2024}} an associate professor leading his lab on the synthesis of 1D and 2D [[nanostructure]]s.<ref name=BIU-chemistry /><ref name=Nessim-Lab>[https://nanosynthesisbiu.webflow.io/ Nessim's Lab]</ref><ref name=Nessim-INREP>[https://inrep.org.il/members/dr-nessim-daniel/ Israel National Research Center for Electrochemiacal Propulsion - Nessim Daniel]</ref>

==Scientific interests and publications==
Nessim's research involves synthesizing and understanding complex growth mechanisms of 1D and 2D nanostructures. Most research is carried using [[chemical vapor deposition]] (CVD)<ref name="Nessim2010">{{cite journal|last1=Nessim|first1=Gilbert D.|title=Properties, synthesis, and growth mechanisms of carbon nanotubes with special focus on thermal chemical vapor deposition|journal=Nanoscale|volume=2|issue=8|year=2010|pages=1306–1323|issn=2040-3364|doi=10.1039/b9nr00427k|pmid=20820718|bibcode=2010Nanos...2.1306N }}</ref> to tune properties and integration of the nanomaterials into various innovative [[energy storage]] and [[electronics|electronic devices]].<ref name="De VolderTawfick2013">{{cite journal|last1=De Volder|first1=Michael F. L.|last2=Tawfick|first2=Sameh H.|last3=Baughman|first3=Ray H.|last4=Hart|first4=A. John|title=Carbon Nanotubes: Present and Future Commercial Applications|journal=Science|volume=339|issue=6119|year=2013|pages=535–539|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.1222453|pmid=23372006|bibcode=2013Sci...339..535D|s2cid=37239907|url=http://mechanosynthesis.mit.edu/journals/076_devolder_13_sciencereview.pdf|archive-date=2017-02-15|access-date=2021-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215085053/http://mechanosynthesis.mit.edu/journals/076_devolder_13_sciencereview.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> These nanostructures include carbon nanotubes (CNTs), carbon fiber-mats (CNFs),<ref name="ShawatPerelshtein2014">{{cite journal|last1=Shawat|first1=Efrat|last2=Perelshtein|first2=Ilana|last3=Westover|first3=Andrew|last4=Pint|first4=Cary L.|last5=Nessim|first5=Gilbert D.|title=Ultra high-yield one-step synthesis of conductive and superhydrophobic three-dimensional mats of carbon nanofibers via full catalysis of unconstrained thin films|journal=J. Mater. Chem. A|volume=2|issue=36|year=2014|pages=15118–15123|issn=2050-7488|doi=10.1039/C4TA02864C}}</ref> [[graphene]],<ref name="MarcianoGonen2016">{{cite journal|last1=Marciano|first1=Ortal|last2=Gonen|first2=Shmuel|last3=Levy|first3=Naomi|last4=Teblum|first4=Eti|last5=Yemini|first5=Reut|last6=Nessim|first6=Gilbert Daniel|last7=Ruthstein|first7=Sharon|last8=Elbaz|first8=Lior|title=Modulation of Oxygen Content in Graphene Surfaces Using Temperature-Programmed Reductive Annealing: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance and Electrochemical Study|journal=Langmuir|volume=32|issue=44|year=2016|pages=11672–11680|issn=0743-7463|doi=10.1021/acs.langmuir.6b02987|pmid=27728764}}</ref> [[graphene oxide]] (GO) reduced GO (rGO), and non-carbon bulk layered materials<ref name="SomekhShawat2014">{{cite journal|last1=Somekh|first1=Miriam|last2=Shawat|first2=Efrat|last3=Nessim|first3=Gilbert D.|title=Fully reproducible, low-temperature synthesis of high-quality, few-layer graphene on nickel via preheating of gas precursors using atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition|journal=J. Mater. Chem. A|volume=2|issue=46|year=2014|pages=19750–19758|issn=2050-7488|doi=10.1039/C4TA03876B}}</ref> like metal -sulfides, -phosphides and -selenides.<ref name="ItzhakTeblum2018">{{cite journal|last1=Itzhak|first1=Anat|last2=Teblum|first2=Eti|last3=Girshevitz|first3=Olga|last4=Okashy|first4=Sivan|last5=Turkulets|first5=Yury|last6=Burlaka|first6=Luba|last7=Cohen-Taguri|first7=Gili|last8=Shawat Avraham|first8=Efrat|last9=Noked|first9=Malachi|last10=Shalish|first10=Ilan|last11=Nessim|first11=Gilbert Daniel|title=Digenite (Cu<sub>9</sub>S<sub>5</sub>): Layered p-Type Semiconductor Grown by Reactive Annealing of Copper|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=30|issue=7|year=2018|pages=2379–2388|issn=0897-4756|doi=10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b00191}}</ref><ref name="KumarAziz2020">{{cite journal|last1=Kumar|first1=Subodh|last2=Aziz|first2=S. K. Tarik|last3=Kumar|first3=Sushil|last4=Riyajuddin|first4=Sk|last5=Yaniv|first5=Gili|last6=Meshi|first6=Louisa|last7=Nessim|first7=Gilbert D.|last8=Ghosh|first8=Kaushik|title=Three-Dimensional Graphene-Decorated Copper-Phosphide (Cu3P@3DG) Heterostructure as an Effective Electrode for a Supercapacitor|journal=Frontiers in Materials|volume=7|year=2020|issn=2296-8016|doi=10.3389/fmats.2020.00030|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Konar2020">{{cite journal|last1=Konar|first1=Rajashree|last2=Rosy|first2=S.|last3=Perelshtein|first3=I.|last4=Teblum|first4=E.|last5=Telkhozhayeva|first5=M.|last6=Tkachev|first6=M.|last7=Richter|first7=J.|last8=Cattaruzza|first8=E.|last9=Pietropolli|first9=A.C|last10=Stoppa|first10=P.|last11=Noked|first11=M.|last12=Nessim|first12=G.D.|title=Scalable Synthesis of Few-Layered 2D Tungsten Diselenide (2H-WSe2) Nanosheets Directly Grown on Tungsten (W) Foil Using Ambient-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition for Reversible Li-Ion Storage|journal=ACS Omega|volume=5|year=2020|issue=31|pages=19409–19421|doi=10.1021/acsomega.0c01155|pmid=32803034|pmc=7424584|doi-access=free}}</ref> In the synthesis of [[carbon nanotube]]s, (CNTs), he has pioneered multiple techniques such as [[Air preheater|gas preheating]], the role of the underlayer, and the use of [[thin film]] reservoirs and overlayers to modulate specific material characteristic parameters such as diameter, length and the number of walls.  In the synthesis of metal [[chalcogenide]]s, he innovated in the synthesis of bulk [[Two-dimensional materials|2D layered materials]].

Among his previous awards were a 2-year [[Intel]] Corporation Fellowship during his PhD.<ref name=BIU-chemistry /> Currently, he is the President of The Israel Vacuum Society (IVS),<ref name=Nessim-IVS>[https://www.ivs.org.il/Templates/ShowPage.asp?DBID=1&TMID=139&LNGID=1&FID=956&PID=0&IID=3577 Gilbert Daniel Nessim - Israel Vacuum Society]{{Dead link|date=November 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> which is aimed at promoting and stimulating professional interconnections and communication among Israeli scientists specializing in the areas of [[surface science]], [[thin film]]s and vacuum science.
